_comment: kiln.world tracked writes: the boundaries where a mod could tell the native service from Kiln.TestKit's fake world.
Read by native/services/world/tests/writes_test.cpp (the native rules), by managed/tests/Kiln.TestKit.Tests
(FakeWorldParityTests: the fake) and by managed/tests/Kiln.Host.Tests (ManifestWritesTests: the managed manifest
reader). A change here changes all three. Names: a string, or {"pattern": "T{i}", "count": n, "from": k}
(T0..). Declaration names: "known:i" is the i-th component type the world has (the native test makes its own
world; the fake's are Kiln.Game's components in name order), "unknown:i" a name the world does not have.
Manifests: valid false means the list is refused and the mod still loads (a warning; each of its tracked writes
answers with what is wrong with the list), as before tracked writes, when "writes" was a key nobody read.

manifests.case: a repeated name is read once, in order
65 copies of one name: every entry counts

declarations.case: unknown names take no accessor: a known name after 92 unknown ones is the program's
the program takes 91 known types in listing order (one of the engine's 92 accessors reads SpawnTime), the 92nd is over the limit
a type two mods list counts once and is each mod's

lifetime.case: a write that waits behind a full update never lands on another entity under the same id (status, reasonContains: its entity lost the component at an update while it waited)

replaced.case: the entity has a generation (SpawnTime) and is made again with another one: refused right before the write
replaced.reasonContains: is not the entity the write was asked for

noGeneration.case: the entity has no SpawnTime: not kept waiting behind a full update, answered at once
